rationale:
ROUND 3 — round 2's gating objection was RIGHT AND IT KILLED MY ROUND-1 FIX. Read this first.

**The objection (editquality, gating):** `unreconciled_declaration` only fires when baseline is nil, but nil required BOTH no lastItem AND no previousRow — and previousRow was prior REGISTER state, the very signal round 2's own rationale named as broken. The register is re-verified DAILY, so a previous evidence_base row essentially always exists carrying the correct value. Baseline was never nil. The first-declaration case never fired. The mechanism was STILL blind to bugs_closed/225 after a whole round spent fixing exactly that. I fixed the symptom and left the cause sitting in the fallback chain, and my tests passed because they tested the fix in isolation rather than against the bug.

**The fix makes the code SMALLER, which is usually the sign of a right answer.** Two questions were conflated:
  'has the register's VALUE moved?'     — answered by comparing successive register rows
  'has this TOOL ever been reconciled?' — answered ONLY by whether we have ever filed for this pair
previousRow answers the first; I was using it for the second. It is DELETED — the map, the query, the loader branch. The baseline is now the newest fact_drift finding for (fact, tool) and nothing else, and its ABSENCE is the never-reconciled signal. The value-move case still works: a moved register value stops matching what the tool was last told. One map, no fallback, no register history read at all.

**PROVEN, and the proving is itself worth reporting because I got it wrong twice.** Mutation M11 (put previousRow back on the struct + loader) PASSED — the test builds factDriftBaselines as a struct literal, so the loader is not on its path. M11b (re-add the history query, assert ExpectationsWereMet) PASSED — sqlmock reports unfulfilled expectations, not extra queries, and my mutation read the row without using it. Only M11c — field declared, POPULATED, and CONSULTED by baselineFor — failed, with the message I wanted: 'a stable register plus a never-reconciled tool must produce exactly one finding, got 0 - this is bugs_closed/225's shape'. I nearly recorded a false proof. There is now a planner-level test that constrains the loader's query set, and a WRONG_CALLS row: an induced red is evidence only if the mutation is FAITHFUL to the defect.

**reuse_agent + tooling_provenance (both medium, same point): reused.** discovery_checks.ToolSubjectKeyExpr is now exported and the fan-out matches it against dp.subject_key instead of hand-writing an equivalent. They were right that a second spelling can drift from what the acceptance tiers resolve. VERIFIED LIVE that the shared expression resolves the motivating tools: loanandmortgagecalculator mortgages-stamp-duty -> 'mortgages-stamp-duty', mortgagecalculator tool-stamp-duty -> 'stamp-duty', both non-fork (which also confirms this round's claim that every live route is human). Note the deliberate asymmetry, documented at the export: the EXPRESSION is reused, toolEligibilityWhere is not, because that predicate admits neither tool.

**guardian (low, x2), measured rather than asserted:** ValidateExperienceCriteria has exactly ONE production caller, write_experience_pattern_action.go:217 — tool PLAN fences are not validated at write time at all, so P11's blast radius is the experience-pattern write path only. And there is no namespace collision: 0 of 161 current doc_plans and 0 of 11 experience_patterns carry a top-level `facts` key.

**tooling_provenance (low): the doc_notes row now EXISTS** — migration 440, applied 2026-08-16, one note on each SDLT subject key recording what the facts key does, the three bands, the routing split, the one-time burst and the two deferrals. Both halves induced: first run wrote 2 notes, second run hit the idempotency guard and skipped both; the verify block RAISEs rather than SELECTs.

**bug_historian (medium): the human-review queue has no working surface (bugs_open/033).** Accepted and named rather than argued away — it is true, it is not this change's defect, and the alternative (auto-fixing a tax calculator on a shared template) is worse. It is recorded in bugs_open/288 §5 as a residual and in the CONTRIB, so nobody reads a filed finding as a fixed one.

**bug_historian (medium): entry==nil and 'checked, unchanged' both read as silence.** Now materially reduced by the baseline change: the unreconciled case fires on the ABSENCE OF A PRIOR FINDING, independent of whether the evidence refresh produced an entry this pass — so a fact whose citation was not attempted this cycle still gets its first-contact reconciliation. What remains conflated is 'refreshed and unchanged' vs 'not attempted' for an ALREADY-reconciled pair, where the outcome is identical (nothing owed) and the distinction costs a per-fact attempt log. Stated, not silently dropped.

— EARLIER ROUND RATIONALE FOLLOWS —

ROUND 2 — round 1 was REVISE and the gating objection was RIGHT. Answering it changed the mechanism, so read the three fixes first.

**1. The gating objection (editquality, high) found that this mechanism would have been blind to its own motivating bug.** The baseline is defined purely from prior REGISTER state, so a tool that is stale on the day it opts in — against a fact whose value has not moved since — yielded baseline == current and emitted nothing. That is exactly bugs_closed/225: correct register, stale code, no subsequent legislative change. I had a test asserting that silence, with a comment justifying it ('is the current number right' is Piece 4's question). The reasoning was true and the behaviour was still wrong: I do not need an oracle to notice that NOBODY HAS EVER CHECKED THIS PAIR — that is a claim about our own records, not about arithmetic. Fixed: a declaration with no baseline files one unreconciled_declaration review item per (fact, tool), self-quieting because the item carries the value that becomes the next pass's baseline. Mutation M8 reverts to the old behaviour and the new test fails, so this is closed by construction.

**2. Risk inversion (compliance, medium), also right.** Every human-routed finding sat at medium/35, ranking a CONFIRMED value move on a no_auto_fix tax calculator BELOW an auto-fixable drift at high/30. The harder a thing is to fix automatically, the more urgent it is. Now three bands: value_drift high/30, evidence_drift medium/35, unreconciled_declaration low/60.

**3. Audit vs liveness predicate (debug_historian, high).** p.status='active' is the estate's liveness predicate and is documented as wrong for choosing which pages to JUDGE. Now uses the shared datahelpers.NeverDeployedPagePredicateFor. The seat's sharpest point was the asymmetry — I had measured the eligibility predicate in that same query and not this one. MEASURED before changing it, and stated honestly: both motivating pages are active/deployed, so the first version would NOT have shipped inert; fleet-wide 198 active tool pages against 6 archived. This closes a door rather than repairing a live miss.

**Answered by measurement or citation rather than by change, each verifiable:** the fact id IS in the item_key (fact_drift:<fact_id>:<subject_key>:<site_id> — my round-1 sketch hid it, which is why bug_historian could not see it, and its bugs_open/091 concern is the right one to raise); a persistently-403 source is NOT permanent silence, because refreshCitationFact marks a fact drifted once it passes staleness_days whether or not the fetch succeeded, and that arrives here as evidence_drift; exactly ONE agent type calls this action (evidence-freshness); scripts/audit-optional-key-budget.sh reports 0 shared actions over the N=10 budget, so P11 does not flip this to architecture scope; a non-fork emission already carries no component id (em.ComponentID is set only under tool.isFork(), and uuid.Parse of "" fails, leaving the column nil).

**One design call the round forced into the open, stated because it has a cost.** Filing per (fact, tool) means seeding a 13-fact fence produces 13 items at once. Collapsing to one item per tool would be tidier and is wrong: a key coarser than the finding drops every finding after the first (bugs_open/091). Kept per-fact, banded low so the burst reads as a backlog rather than 13 alerts, and named in the CONTRIB so the receiving lane is not surprised.

**Still unaddressed, deliberately, and named rather than silent:** the three claims.go exemptions (script, tool-page prose, currency) are untouched — closing them needs a retired-figure scan over raw deployed HTML, which is a second scanner over the same components (bugs_open/093's shape) and needs a measured false-positive rate first; RFC_025's artifact_check stays unreachable for citation facts (stage 2b, adjacent but it changes an existing mechanism's semantics and deserves its own round); Piece 4, the oracle that would answer 'is the figure RIGHT', stays behind its RFC. All three are residual in bugs_open/288 §5.

— ORIGINAL ROUND 1 RATIONALE FOLLOWS —

bugs_open/225 — the evidence register guards COPY, not CODE, and a calculator ran an expired tax rule for sixteen months while every check passed. mortgagecalculator.co.uk's SDLT tool encoded the first-time-buyer relief cap that expired 2025-03-31; the site's prose and band table were correct, only the JS constant was stale. Nothing in the platform could catch it, and the three reasons are all deliberate design decisions: datahelpers/claims.go's nonAssertionElements drops <script> from every claims scan; editorialPageTypes exempts tool pages from the numeric arm; isExcludedNumber drops currency, so even the figure stated in finance PROSE is scanned by nothing. The one mechanism that reads raw rendered_html against the register (RFC_025's artifact_check) has zero consumers across 130 facts fleet-wide, is unreachable for citation-sourced facts (the citation branch continues before the artifact_check test), and is addressed by a component_id that had already died for this bug's own page when it was decomposed.

Meanwhile the register on that site carries 13 GOV.UK-cited SDLT facts, re-verified daily, whose governing_rule says in terms: 'A calculator is a claim about legislation: when a fact here changes or its citation is lost, every tool that encodes it is suspect until re-verified.' Nothing joined a fact to a tool. This change is that join, and it is not a new design: it is Pieces 2 and 3 of an owner-visible plan already in the repo (mortgagecalculator_couk_adoption/PLAN_2026-08-09_facts_into_tool_acceptance.md), whose Piece 1 is live as migration 366 / CLM-021. Piece 4 (an oracle computing expectations from the register) stays behind its RFC and is explicitly NOT in this change.

OPT-IN BY DATA, unsafe default OFF: until a tool's criteria fence carries a `facts` list, this code costs one extra SELECT per register-bearing site per day and changes nothing — no new action config key, no exported symbol changed, no schema change, no migration. Under the owner's RFC_022 narrowing (opt-in, unsafe side default OFF, zero live consumers — enumerated: 0 of 130 facts and 0 of 87 current tool PLANs declare anything today) this is council scope, not architecture scope.

THE PART I MOST WANT REVIEWED is the routing split, because getting it wrong is worse than not building it. A moved VALUE routes to tool-improver ONLY when a tool-level component owns the page's code AND the fence does not say no_auto_fix. Everything else — a non-fork page, a no_auto_fix fence, and EVERY evidence-only drift (citation lost, artefact changed) — routes to a human via a new handler-less fact_drift_review item. A fetch error routes to nobody at all. Two things drove that: bugs_open/281/TL-042 (tool-improver rewrites the SHARED template of a non-fork; one finding did exactly that fleet-wide on 2026-08-05 and again on 08-14), and bugs_open/126 (a false failure aimed an automated rewriter at a tool's disclaimer — here the target would be arithmetic on a page quoting tax law). Note the honest consequence: both live SDLT fences carry no_auto_fix and neither page is a fork, so on today's fleet EVERY route is human and the improve_tool arm is proven by unit test only. I would rather ship it that way than widen the auto-fix door.

MEASURED, and it changed the design: the fan-out deliberately does NOT use the acceptance ladder's toolEligibilityWhere predicate. Run live 2026-08-16, that predicate admits NEITHER tool this mechanism exists for — mortgagecalculator's tool-stamp-duty page carries two components and loanandmortgagecalculator's mortgages-stamp-duty three since its B2 decomposition, and the sole-component clause excludes both. Keying on eligibility would have produced a check that could never fire on the tools that motivated it, and it would have read green. It uses the platform's own name rule instead — the one Tier 4 already uses to resolve a tool's URL.

Every routing guard has a test that FAILS when the guard is removed: six mutations run, six reds, restored green (no_auto_fix, fork, evidence-vs-value, fetch-error, baseline-present, baseline-precedence), plus a seventh on the validator rule. The no-op path is asserted too — a site with no declaration costs exactly one SELECT and its result JSON is byte-identical to before.

plan.summary: Join the evidence register to the tools that encode its facts. Piece 2: a tool's criteria fence may carry a fence-level `facts` list of register fact ids (ids only, never values — PBP-037's rule), shape-checked by a new validator rule P11. Piece 3: the daily evidence-freshness sweep resolves each site's declaring PLANs to its pages and files one work item per (fact, tool) that is owed something — improve_tool only where a fixer may safely act, a new handler-less fact_drift_review otherwise, and nothing at all on a fetch error. Opt-in by register/fence data; inert until a fence declares.

edits.rationale: Piece 2's parser. FENCE-LEVEL, not per-check: a tool encodes a fact, a check does not, and a per-check key stays refused by the validator's existing P7 inert-field rule. IDS ONLY, never values — pinning a value in a fleet-global doc_plans row (which has no site_id) would recreate the very failure the plan calls F3, a golden that defends a wrong number. FAIL-OPEN on absent/unparseable criteria, exactly like parseNoAutoFix beside it, so a fence that never mentioned facts cannot become an error elsewhere; a present-but-MALFORMED declaration returns issues so it is visibly ignored rather than silently dropped. Kept out of acceptanceFenceFlags deliberately: that struct is the judge's view, and a malformed facts value must not make parseNoAutoFix fail-open on a fence that set no_auto_fix correctly.

P11: refuse a malformed `facts` declaration WHERE IT IS WRITTEN rather than silently ignoring it on the day a fact moves — which is bugs_open/225's failure shape one rung higher. Placed after P5 and before the checks loop, so P7 still owns the per-check case. Nine lines, no behaviour change for any fence without the key. The doc comment's P1..P10 list gains P11, including the sentence that the key is read only by refresh_evidence_base and asserted by neither tier — so an author cannot read a green fence as 'the figures were compared'.

edits.symbol: loadFactDriftIndex / loadFactDriftBaselines (ROUND 3: previousRow deleted, ToolSubjectKeyExpr reused)
edits.rationale: The site->PLAN->page join and the baseline. ONE query per register-bearing site, pre-filtered on the fence text; zero rows ends the pass. It resolves by the platform's OWN name rule (p.name IN (subject_key, 'tool-'||subject_key), plus a tool-level component whose function is the subject key) — the rule Tier 4 already uses for a tool's URL — and NOT by toolEligibilityWhere, which was measured live and admits neither of the two tools this exists for (both are multi-component pages). Fact ids resolve against the swept SITE's register, never the fleet-global PLAN (doc_plans has no site_id); an id the register does not carry is inert and reported, never fatal. The baseline is 'the value the tool was last TOLD': the latest fact_drift item's spec.fact.new_value for that (fact, tool), else the same fact's value in the site's PREVIOUS evidence_base row, else nothing fires. Read as a raw map, never through the typed EvidenceBase, which does not model citation/writer_line/unit. A per-fact 'last swept value' key in the register was rejected: it would make a consumer the author of a human-owned row.

ROUND 2: adds the first-declaration case the council's gating objection demanded. The routing decision, pure and unit-testable in isolation (the shape a council objection forced on shouldRaiseStaleEvidence in the RFC_025 round, reused here deliberately). VALUE DRIFT -> improve_tool only when the page has a tool-level component AND the fence has no no_auto_fix; otherwise fact_drift_review with the reason recorded (not_a_fork / no_auto_fix). EVIDENCE DRIFT -> always human: a lost GOV.UK quote is not evidence a figure moved. FETCH ERROR -> reported, filed nowhere (CLM-008: unknown is not loss; an item on every 403 day trains people to ignore the queue). Two distinct item_key prefixes because refreshOnConflict rewrites an open item's summary and spec but never its type or handler — one prefix would let an open review item silently absorb a later auto-fixable finding.
edits.sketch:
switch {
// ROUND 2 — without this the mechanism is blind to bugs_closed/225's own shape
case hasVal && baseline == nil:
    em.Kind = "unreconciled_declaration"
    em.NewValue = &newVal
    em.Route, em.Reason = "fact_drift_review", "never_reconciled"
    // self-quieting: this item's new_value becomes the next pass's baseline
case hasVal && baseline != nil && math.Abs(newVal-*baseline) > 1e-9:
    em.Kind = "value_drift"
    switch {
    case !tool.isFork():  em.Route, em.Reason = "fact_drift_review", "not_a_fork"
    case tool.NoAutoFix:  em.Route, em.Reason = "fact_drift_review", "no_auto_fix"
    default:              em.Route = "improve_tool"
    }
case entry != nil && entry.Outcome == "drifted":
    em.Kind, em.Route, em.Reason = "evidence_drift", "fact_drift_review", "evidence_drift"
case entry != nil && entry.Outcome == "error":
    em.Kind, em.Outcome = "skipped_unknown", "none"   // filed nowhere; staleness_days escalates instead
    return em, true
default:
    return em, false
}

edits.rationale: The write half, one transaction per emission, through the SHARED writeWorkItem with refreshOnConflict (not a hand-rolled INSERT — the fork that bugs_open/091 was filed about). Each item carries page_id and, for a fork, component_id in the COLUMNS as well as the spec, because tool-improver's load_tool pre-flight hard-fails without page_id. The issue text is the payload the fixer actually reads ({{.input_data.issue}}), so it carries the fact id, old->new with unit, the register's own writer_line with {value} substituted, and the source URL — and, on a human route, the reason and what to do instead (re-file needs_tool_recreation, whose builder reads the register per CLM-021; never improve_tool, whose component_id would be the shared wrapper).

Two wiring lines and two omitempty result fields. The fan-out is PLANNED before the dry-run return (so a dry run reports exactly what it would file — that is how the live proof is run without writing) and WRITTEN after the two existing raises, so it cannot change when they fire. It never touches `changed`, res.Drifted, res.ArtifactCheckDrifted or shouldRaiseStaleEvidence: the RFC_025 round's architecture objection was that decoupling the citation raise altered behaviour for every existing caller, and that gate is left exactly as it is. A citation-only drift with nothing else changed still raises no site item; the per-tool item fires on its own trigger and its own key. EncodedByTools is stamped on drifted entries only, omitempty, so a site with no declarations marshals byte-identically to before (asserted by a test).
